items.title: Port Talbot Steelworks: draft permit decision (PAN-029148.1)
items.time: Closed 13 November 2026. No decision published by 23 November 2026.
items.plain: Tata Steel is changing the steelworks permit as it moves from blast furnaces to an electric arc furnace. NRW is minded to approve this first stage and wants comments on the draft permit.
items.detail: Names Port Talbot directly: the site is Port Talbot Steelworks, SA13 2NG, and NRW lists Aberavon, Baglan, Bryn and Cwmavon, Margam, Port Talbot, Sandfields East and West and Tai-bach among the areas covered. This variation (V019 of permit EPR/BL7108IM) removes blast furnace and basic oxygen steelmaking activities, mothballs others during the transformation and adds new steam boilers (medium combustion plant). NRW says it can only consider comments within its legal permitting remit. Later stages, including the electric arc furnace itself, will be consulted on separately. The consultation closed on 13 November 2026. No decision on the final permit had been published by 23 November 2026.
items.how: The consultation has closed. Watch NRW's consultation hub and public register for the decision.

people: Residents of Aberavon, Baglan, Margam, Sandfields and Tai-bach near the site
systems: Air quality and emissions from the works

items.title: Revising the National Development Framework
items.time: Closed 20 November 2026. The Welsh Government consultations list shows it as closed, awaiting outcome (checked 23 November).
items.plain: The Welsh Government is starting to revise Wales's national planning framework, and asks how people want to take part and what the new framework should do.
items.detail: Applies to all of Wales; it does not name a Neath Port Talbot place. Kept because the National Development Framework guides large developments, energy and growth areas across Wales, including this county borough. It covers the draft Statement of Public Participation, the draft National Conversation Engagement Plan and the role of the revised framework. Closed on 20 November 2026; the Welsh Government lists it as awaiting outcome.
items.how: The consultation has closed. Watch the consultation page for the Welsh Government's summary of responses.

people: Landowners and businesses near future development

items.title: Draft Taxi Licensing Policy
items.time: Closes at 12 noon on Thursday 26 November 2026, as stated on the council's consultations page.
items.plain: The council is updating the rules for taxi and private hire drivers, vehicles and operators. Changes are marked in red in the draft policy.
items.detail: Neath Port Talbot Council licenses hackney carriage and private hire drivers, vehicles and operators across the county borough. The revised policy (August 2026) sets the standards and procedures the council uses when deciding licence applications. The council asks residents, the licensed trade and partner organisations for comments.
items.how: Read the revised policy (PDF) and comment through the 'Have your say' link on the council's consultations page before 12 noon on 26 November 2026.

people: Taxi and private hire drivers and operators (businesses)
Older and disabled passengers who rely on taxis

items.title: Afan Forest draft Forest Resource Plan
items.time: closing time not published; the NRW consultation hub lists the Afan Forest Resource Plan as closing 30 November 2026 (checked 23 November).
items.plain: NRW sets out how it plans to manage Afan Forest for the next 10 years: timber, nature recovery, climate resilience and recreation, including the mountain bike trails.
items.detail: Names Neath Port Talbot places: the plan covers the Afan, Pelenna, Corrwg and Drysiog catchments, with a drop-in at Afan Visitor Centre, Cynonville, Port Talbot. Proposals include more diverse woodland, better ecological connectivity, restoring peatland and ancient woodland, managing invasive species, improving river habitats and protecting water and soil. The NRW consultation hub confirms the 30 November 2026 close.
items.how: View the documents and respond online (link in the NRW news release), go to the drop-in on 11 November, or email frp@cyfoethnaturiolcymru.gov.uk.

people: Forest businesses and mountain bike tourism

items.title: Swansea Bay and West Wales Metro: rail proposals
items.body: Transport for Wales (with Neath Port Talbot and neighbouring councils)
items.time: closing time not published; the Transport for Wales page still gives no closing date (checked 23 November). The 3 November to 13 December dates come from local news reports (Nation.Cymru and others, 3 November 2026). The Neath Railway Station drop-in was on 20 November; the last listed drop-ins are in Swansea on 25 and 26 November.
items.plain: Plans for more frequent trains and possible new stations across the region, including a new service running through Neath with connections there to Cardiff. No funding is guaranteed yet.
items.detail: Names Neath Port Talbot: Transport for Wales says it is developing the metro with Neath Port Talbot, Swansea, Carmarthenshire and Pembrokeshire councils, and the second phase would run new services via Neath, with a public drop-in at Neath Railway Station on 20 November. Proposed new stations include Llandarcy, Landore, Winsh-wen, Morriston, Felindre, Pont-lliw and Cockett. Delivery depends on UK Government funding. A separate possible light rail or tram-train between Swansea and Neath is not part of this consultation. The closing date is from a news report, not the TfW page; check the survey page.
items.how: Take the online survey on the Transport for Wales Have Your Say page, or go to a remaining drop-in event in Swansea (Cockett Community Centre, 25 November; Quadrant Shopping Centre, 26 November).

people: Rail passengers and people who travel to work, school or medical appointments
Older and disabled people who rely on accessible stations
Neighbours of proposed stations and new track near the site
groups: Town and community councils near proposed stations
systems: Walking and cycling routes to stations

items.title: Restricting the sale of high-caffeine energy drinks to children: enforcement
items.time: closing time not published; the consultation page says submit comments by 17 December 2026.
items.plain: The Welsh Government is going ahead with a ban on selling high-caffeine energy drinks to under-16s, and asks how it should be enforced: age checks, compliance checks, penalties and monitoring.
items.detail: Applies to all of Wales; it does not name a Neath Port Talbot place. Kept because it would apply in every shop and vending machine in the county borough, and enforcement would fall to local councils' trading standards teams (my reading; the page talks about enforcement generally). Launched 5 November 2026.
items.how: Respond online, or email the response form to WiderDeterminantsOfHealthBranch@gov.wales, or post it to Wider Determinants of Health Branch, Public Health Directorate, Welsh Government, Cathays Park, Cardiff CF10 3NQ, by 17 December 2026.

items.title: Shaping Mid and West Wales Fire and Rescue Service Together
items.body: Mid and West Wales Fire and Rescue Service

items.title: Maintenance dredging at Monkstone marina, River Neath (marine licence DML2629)
items.body: Natural Resources Wales (application by Monkstone Cruising & Sailing Club Ltd)
items.time: Closed 18 November 2026. The NRW consultation hub lists it under closed activities (checked 23 November).
items.plain: The sailing club wants a licence to dredge its marina about every three years and release the dredged material into the River Neath on ebb tides. NRW is taking comments or objections.
items.detail: Names the River Neath and Monkstone marina; the marina is at Jersey Marine in Neath Port Talbot (the location within the county borough is my reading; the notice names only the marina and the river). The dredging would lower the marina to 2.2 m below the gate cill, a 1.2 m reduction. Application documents are on NRW's public register under reference DML2629. The notice opened on 20 October 2026. Representations are shared with the applicant and may be published with personal details removed. The notice closed on 18 November 2026; no licence decision had been published by 23 November 2026.
items.how: The notice has closed. Watch NRW's public register under reference DML2629 for the licence decision.

groups: Conservation groups watching the Neath estuary
systems: River Neath estuary: sediment and water quality

items.title: Margam Connection community fund: help decide how £1.06 million is spent
items.time: closing time not published; National Grid's press release of 4 November 2026 says the online survey is open until 26 November (checked 23 November).
items.plain: National Grid is putting £1.06 million into a community fund for Port Talbot alongside the new substations that will power the steelworks' electric arc furnace, and asks what the money should support.
items.detail: Names Port Talbot and Margam: the fund accompanies the Margam Connection project, which extends a substation off Harbour Way, builds another inside the steelworks and links them by underground cable. Suggested priorities include skills and training, green spaces, community facilities, youth services, help with fuel bills and support for local firms, and people can propose their own. Drop-ins were held on 6 and 7 November. National Grid has not said who will decide between bids or when money will first be paid. Sources: National Grid press release and Swansea News, both 4 November 2026.
items.how: Fill in the survey linked from National Grid's project page for the Margam Connection by 26 November 2026. It is open to residents, businesses, charities, community groups and councillors.

groups: Town and community councils and local councillors
systems: Electricity grid connection for the steelworks

items.title: Dog access rules for Aberavon Beach and Promenade, 2027 to 2029
items.time: Cabinet is due to make the final decision on 2 December 2026, according to the council's press release of 10 November 2026.
items.plain: After a public consultation with 2,191 responses, councillors are choosing new dog rules for Aberavon Beach and Promenade. Officers suggest a smaller dog-free area on the beach and dogs on leads on the promenade all year.
items.detail: Names Aberavon Beach and Promenade. The current Public Spaces Protection Orders expire on 5 March 2027. Beach options: keep the existing dog exclusion area, reduce it while keeping the main bathing area dog-free (officers' preferred option, which they say keeps Blue Flag status possible), remove it, or allow dogs at set times. Promenade options: dogs on leads from 1 May to 30 September as now, or all year (officers' preferred option). 64% of respondents opposed reinstating the existing beach exclusion and 36% supported it; about 70% of respondents were dog owners. The Visible Services and Streetscene Scrutiny Committee considered the report on 13 November 2026; its outcome could not be checked because the council's committee papers site could not be read automatically.
items.how: The consultation has closed. You can contact your local councillor before Cabinet meets on 2 December 2026, and read the report on the council's committee papers site.

people: Dog owners and walkers using Aberavon Beach and Promenade
Beach visitors and families using the bathing area
systems: Beach and bathing water (Blue Flag status)

items.title: New Local Development Plan delayed: public consultation moved to late 2027
items.time: Full council is due to consider the new timetable at 1pm on Wednesday 25 November 2026 (Swansea Bay News, 21 November; the council's meetings feed lists the 25 November Council agenda).
items.plain: The council's plan for where new homes and businesses can go runs out on 31 December. Councillors are asked to agree that the public consultation on its replacement moves to November and December 2027, after the May 2027 council elections.
items.detail: Covers the whole county borough. Under the proposed timetable, consultation on the draft (deposit) plan would run in November and December 2027, an independent examination from May to September 2028 and adoption in December 2028; the council says the later dates are a guide only. Reasons given include working out how protected marine conservation areas limit where building can go, newer population and household projections, checking that earmarked sites can still be built, and rising building costs. The draft strategy names Pontardawe and Glynneath as valley hubs for growth and earmarks up to 900 more homes at Coed Hirwaun. If councillors agree, the timetable goes to the Welsh Government for approval. All details are from a Swansea Bay News report of 21 November 2026; the council report itself was not opened because the committee papers site could not be read automatically.
items.how: No consultation is open yet. Watch the council's environment and planning consultations portal; the main public consultation is now proposed for November and December 2027.

people: Residents near housing sites such as Coed Hirwaun and Bryncoch
groups: Town and community councils such as Blaenhonddan
wildlife: Marine and coastal wildlife in protected conservation areas
systems: Green spaces and land use across the borough
